{"path": "src/listpack.c", "lines": "500-560 of 2803", "content": "500: /* Return the number of elements inside the listpack. This function attempts
501:  * to use the cached value when within range, otherwise a full scan is
502:  * needed. As a side effect of calling this function, the listpack header
503:  * could be modified, because if the count is found to be already within
504:  * the 'numele' header field range, the new value is set. */
505: unsigned long lpLength(unsigned char *lp) {
506:     uint32_t numele = lpGetNumElements(lp);
507:     if (numele != LP_HDR_NUMELE_UNKNOWN) return numele;
508: 
509:     /* Too many elements inside the listpack. We need to scan in order
510:      * to get the total number. */
511:     uint32_t count = 0;
512:     unsigned char *p = lpFirst(lp);
513:     while(p) {
514:         count++;
515:         p = lpNext(lp,p);
516:     }
517: 
518:     /* If the count is again within range of the header numele field,
519:      * set it. */
520:     if (count < LP_HDR_NUMELE_UNKNOWN) lpSetNumElements(lp,count);
521:     return count;
522: }
523: 
524: /* Return the listpack element pointed by 'p'.
525:  *
526:  * The function changes behavior depending on the passed 'intbuf' value.
527:  * Specifically, if 'intbuf' is NULL:
528:  *
529:  * If the element is internally encoded as an integer, the function returns
530:  * NULL and populates the integer value by reference in 'count'. Otherwise if
531:  * the element is encoded as a string a pointer to the string (pointing inside
532:  * the listpack itself) is returned, and 'count' is set to the length of the
533:  * string.
534:  *
535:  * If instead 'intbuf' points to a buffer passed by the caller, that must be
536:  * at least LP_INTBUF_SIZE bytes, the function always returns the element as
537:  * it was a string (returning the pointer to the string and setting the
538:  * 'count' argument to the string length by reference). However if the element
539:  * is encoded as an integer, the 'intbuf' buffer is used in order to store
540:  * the string representation.
541:  *
542:  * The user should use one or the other form depending on what the value will
543:  * be used for. If there is immediate usage for an integer value returned
544:  * by the function, than to pass a buffer (and convert it back to a number)
545:  * is of course useless.
546:  *
547:  * If 'entry_size' is not NULL, *entry_size is set to the entry length of the
548:  * listpack element pointed by 'p'. This includes the encoding bytes, length
549:  * bytes, the element data itself, and the backlen bytes.
550:  *
551:  * If the function is called against a badly encoded ziplist, so that there
552:  * is no valid way to parse it, the function returns like if there was an
553:  * integer encoded with value 12345678900000000 + <unrecognized byte>, this may
554:  * be an hint to understand that something is wrong. To crash in this case is
555:  * not sensible because of the different requirements of the application using
556:  * this lib.
557:  *
558:  * Similarly, there is no error returned since the listpack normally can be
559:  * assumed to be valid, so that would be a very high API cost. */
560: static inline unsigned char *lpGetWithSize(unsigned char *p, int64_t *count, unsigned char *intbuf, uint64_t *entry_size) {"}
